findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-preference screenshot is visually identical to light mode; computed color-scheme is normal and the 211 KB DOM/CSS capture contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: No high-contrast or forced-colours adaptation is defined.
findings.evidence: The full DOM/CSS capture contains no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rules, while the UI relies on pale blue and grey low-emphasis text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast adaptations and preserve visible borders/focus indicators.

findings.summary: Full-page navigation swaps have no transition continuity.
findings.evidence: The MPA uses ordinary PHP links and the captured CSS contains no view-transition-name or @view-transition declarations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin board/list/detail navigation, with reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no position-aware navigation or progress cue.
findings.evidence: Full-page mobile captures span several screens, but the header remains ordinary top-of-document chrome and captured CSS has no scroll-state or progress implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact sticky header or unobtrusive scroll progress/return affordance that reacts to position.

findings.summary: Navigation panels clip at narrow viewport edges.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show left-side navigation cut off outside the viewport; no anchor positioning or fallback positions appear in captured CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Use anchored popovers with position-try fallbacks, or a responsive in-flow mobile navigation drawer.

findings.summary: The topic/navigation disclosure is custom and not expressed with semantic disclosure primitives.
findings.evidence: The recon exposes dozens of #none links for topic choices while the DOM contains no dialog, popover, or details primitives.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a button controlling a popover/details disclosure, preserve keyboard semantics, and use real hrefs for navigable topics.

findings.summary: Ads, side rails, and empty reserved regions dominate the content canvas.
findings.evidence: Homepage, listing, and article screenshots devote large areas to side rails, empty ad slots, and peripheral modules; primary content is comparatively narrow.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse unfilled ad slots and simplify side rails, especially on small screens, so the main list/article dominates.

findings.summary: Mobile visitors receive a scaled desktop canvas instead of a responsive layout.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 the layout primitive reports no viewport meta; Chrome renders a 1440 CSS-pixel viewport at scale 0.25. The stats template overflows by 265px and screenshots show tiny desktop UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid width=device-width viewport, remove fixed desktop widths, and rebuild templates with intrinsic fluid grids that reflow at narrow widths.

findings.summary: Reusable cards, tables, and sidebars do not adapt to their available container.
findings.evidence: All mobile archetypes preserve desktop multi-column geometry; the 211 KB CSS capture contains no @container rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and container queries that stack/collapse list, article, and stats components.

findings.summary: Many targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The platform probe measures visible controls such as login at 33x14px, join at 44x14px, topic rows around 22px high, and icon links 24px wide, below common 44px touch guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Give interactive targets at least a 44px hit area, retain visible :focus-visible outlines, and avoid hover-only access.

findings.summary: The homepage’s primary purpose and next action are buried by competing modules.
findings.evidence: The first viewport is mostly navigation, flyouts, ads, and multiple equally weighted board modules; headings are empty in the recon and no clear primary heading describes the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a meaningful H1 and prioritize board discovery/search above secondary news, ads, and promotional modules.

findings.summary: The sampled homepage load paints very late.
findings.evidence: The trace summary reports FCP and LCP at 14,786 ms from navigation start, far outside the good LCP range; the capture also encountered intermittent empty responses.
findings.suggestedFix: Stabilize document delivery, prioritize the LCP resource, and defer ads/secondary modules until core content is visible.

findings.summary: The stats and listing templates shift substantially after load.
findings.evidence: Layout observation reports CLS 0.244 on stats and 0.110 on the listing, including a 0.201 single shift on stats.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions for images/ads/modules and avoid inserting late rows or banners above existing content.

findings.summary: Document delivery is slow, uncompressed, and explicitly uncacheable.
findings.evidence: The HAR summary records a 183,748-byte uncompressed HTML document; HTTP recon reports no-cache/no-store and the trace load event completes around 14.8s.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable Brotli/gzip, remove unnecessary HTML, use appropriate caching, and shorten the critical network chain.

findings.summary: The page ships a large legacy and advertising script surface.
findings.evidence: Rendered recon lists about 40 script tags, including repeated adsbygoogle loads, multiple adstream scripts, jQuery latest, jQuery UI, and cookie helpers.
findings.suggestedFix: Deduplicate ad loaders, remove unused legacy dependencies, and conditionally load below-fold/third-party modules.

findings.summary: Search and several image/icon links lack robust accessible names.
findings.evidence: Recon shows the visible search input has no associated label, and the platform probe counts two empty links without text, aria-label, or an img with alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a programmatic search label, name icon-only links, and audit all image links/controls with axe against the real page.

findings.summary: Small low-emphasis text is difficult to distinguish.
findings.evidence: Screenshots show dense 12px grey and pale-blue text on white/light-grey surfaces; computed DOM evidence includes pale rgb(207,219,245) text.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure all text/UI pairs and raise them to WCAG AA contrast, using larger text where density permits.

findings.summary: Document structure does not expose meaningful headings and landmarks.
findings.evidence: Recon reports an empty H1 and empty H2/H3 elements; computed DOM selectors find no header, nav, or main elements on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive H1, logical section headings, and header/nav/main/footer landmarks; preserve visible focus order.

findings.summary: Mobile text is rendered at an unusably tiny effective size.
findings.evidence: At 360px the browser scales the 1440px desktop layout to 25%; screenshots make board rows and footer text extremely small.
findings.suggestedFix: Use responsive typography and line lengths after fixing viewport/reflow; avoid 12px dense text for primary content.

findings.summary: The mobile experience prevents practical reflow and offers undersized targets.
findings.evidence: The legitimate page probe finds no viewport meta and the layout renders at scale 0.25; many measured targets are 14–24px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scalable viewport, support 320px reflow and 200–400% zoom, and enlarge target hit areas.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and responsive delivery metadata.
findings.evidence: The platform probe finds nearly all visible images without width/height attributes; repeated 405px source images are also displayed at 93px without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio, generate responsive srcset/sizes, and preserve correct aspect ratios.

findings.summary: The page retains a legacy dependency and markup profile.
findings.evidence: Recon includes IE=edge, jquery-latest.js, jQuery UI, jQuery cookie, many inline scripts, and image-based GIF navigation assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Pin and update dependencies, remove obsolete IE-era code, replace legacy image UI with semantic HTML/CSS, and verify BFCache/deprecation health.

findings.summary: Many topic links are not crawlable destinations and mobile metadata is missing.
findings.evidence: Recon contains dozens of anchors resolving to #none/#, while the layout probe reports no viewport meta. robots.txt also disallows all unspecified user agents.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real hrefs for categories, add a valid mobile viewport, and define an explicit crawler policy consistent with public discovery goals.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap/indexing signals are inconsistent or absent.
findings.evidence: The homepage probe finds no canonical link; /sitemap.xml returns a generic “page not found” HTML document with HTTP 200, and robots.txt blocks unspecified agents.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a real XML sitemap with correct status/content type, add canonical URLs, and align robots rules with intended indexing.

findings.summary: Article/entity pages lack structured data.
findings.evidence: The homepage has Open Graph tags, but the rendered probe finds zero JSON-LD blocks and the representative post template exposes no Article structured-data evidence.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org WebSite/Organization and DiscussionForumPosting or Article JSON-LD matching visible content.

findings.summary: HTTPS is used without core security headers.
findings.evidence: The header primitive confirms HTTPS but reports missing CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The public page loads a broad advertising and analytics surface.
findings.evidence: Recon lists Google Tag Manager/gtag, multiple AdSense publishers, contentsfeed adstream endpoints, linkback, and AceCounter among roughly 40 scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory third parties, remove redundant trackers/ad loaders, gate non-essential processing on consent, and minimize transmitted identifiers.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: The security-header audit finds no HSTS, clickjacking defense, CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy on the main document.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors, referrer/permissions policies, and evaluate Trusted Types for inline-script-heavy surfaces.

findings.summary: Navigation state is fragile at narrow edges.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show side navigation clipped outside the viewport, while the site intermittently returned ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE during repeated evidence loads.
findings.suggestedFix: Make menus reflow/reposition within the viewport and ensure async/ad failures cannot block core content.

findings.summary: The document does not declare its Korean language.
findings.evidence: The legitimate rendered homepage probe reports an empty html lang and dir, despite Korean page content.
findings.suggestedFix: Set lang="ko" on the root element and use logical CSS properties so reading direction and translation remain robust.

findings.summary: Legacy, non-responsive imagery wastes bytes and layout work.
findings.evidence: The platform probe shows GIF/JPG assets, no srcset, missing intrinsic dimensions, and 405px images reused at 93px display width.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where appropriate, generate srcset/sizes, and reserve dimensions.

findings.summary: Repeated advertising and legacy scripts create avoidable work.
findings.evidence: Recon lists repeated AdSense/adstream scripts plus GTM, gtag, linkback, AceCounter, jQuery, and jQuery UI on a primarily text/list page.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate analytics, deduplicate loaders, defer below-fold ads, and remove libraries not required for core reading/navigation.

findings.summary: Third-party code is disproportionate to the core forum experience.
findings.evidence: A text-centric portal includes numerous ad/analytics origins and repeated third-party loaders before any user interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party request/byte budget, lazy-load non-essential ads, and measure each vendor’s user value and carbon/performance cost.

taskList.title: Semantic headings, landmarks, labels, and targets
Crawlable links, canonical, sitemap, and structured data
Reduce ads, empty chrome, and legacy asset/script waste
